transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I came in because... well, I'm having a really hard time keeping my focus at work. I'm a physical scientist, and lately, I just can't keep my mind on the actual experiments I'm supposed to be running. Like, I'll be in the middle of an important grant call or a safety meeting, and I'll notice something totally unrelated—a pump vibrating, or a side comment from one of the students, or even just some odd peak in an old data spectrum. And then, suddenly, I'm off chasing that one tiny thing for hours. Meanwhile, the actual project that everyone is waiting on me for just completely falls apart. It's becoming a serious problem.
Did you have these kinds of focus problems as a child?

No, not really. I mean, I don't remember ever having trouble with it back then. I was actually pretty focused in school as a kid. This... this feels completely different. It's really just been lately that my mind has been jumping all over the place like this.
Have you had a period recently when you felt unusually energetic or needed much less sleep than usual?

Yes, actually. I've noticed a big change with my sleep lately. Most nights, I'm only getting maybe two or three hours. Half the time I just end up passing out on the couch with my laptop still open. But the weird thing is, I don't feel tired at all. I wake up feeling completely sharp and just... ready to get back to work. It honestly feels like sleeping is just this inefficient interruption to everything I need to be doing.
During this time, have you been feeling unusually high or euphoric?

I don't know if I'd use the word euphoric, but... for months now, I've felt almost electrified. It's like everything in the lab is finally moving at my speed. 

But on the flip side of that, if someone questions my plan or tells me I need to slow down, I just... I snap at them. I get incredibly irritated. It's actually gotten bad enough that I've noticed the grad students are starting to avoid my office entirely.
During this period, have you been taking on a lot more projects or work than usual?

Yes, absolutely. I'm at the lab way before anyone else even arrives. I've been rewriting our protocols, rearranging all the instrument schedules, emailing collaborators in three different countries... I'm just starting all these new analyses at the exact same time. It honestly feels like if I just sit still, I'm wasting the one chance I have to fix everything.
During this time, have you felt more powerful, important, or unusually certain that your ideas are exceptional or that you can accomplish things others can't?

Yes, I did. I mean... I genuinely believed I could rescue the entire multi-site project all by myself. I was completely certain that I needed to redesign the whole spectroscopy approach, and that I could mentor every single student in the lab better than their own advisors. I just knew I could pull all of that off and still beat the grant deadline... if people would just stop getting in my way and let me work.
Has this period caused serious problems at work or in your relationships?

Yes, it has. It's actually gotten to the point where my department had to step in. They took away decisions I used to handle on my own. I guess I was missing important priorities and my scheduling was all over the place. Plus, with the way I was acting with the students... they said my supervision was straining things and putting the whole project, and even lab safety expectations, at risk.
During this period, have you had beliefs that other people said were clearly not true or unrealistic?

No, I don't think so. I mean, they told me I was taking on too much and being unrealistic about the timeline, but I didn't have any strange beliefs or anything like that. I just thought I could work faster than I actually could. Nobody ever said I was believing things that were completely untrue.
